item.title: Bridges & Brunch with Strasburg Scooter Tours — Fri Jul 24 — Strasburg Scooter Tours
item.description:
Experience a relaxing morning ride through the back roads of Amish Country in Lancaster County, PA. Along the way to a 19th century covered bridge, enjoy the scenery of rolling hills, breathtaking views, and our Amish neighbors going about their daily routines. Itinerary Duration: 1.5-2 hours Some of our past tours have included:
A guided tour of one of Lancaster County’s most beautiful covered bridges An opportunity for a close up of daily life in Amish Country $10 dining voucher to one of two of Strasburg’s favorites brunch spots, Casey Jones’ Restaurant and Speckled Hen*
And each trip is unique, so you never know what we might have in store for you! *Unfortunately, we regret to inform you that some of the food offerings on the tour may not be considered ‘Kosher.’ We apologize for any inconvenience.

item.title: PNCR Outdoors All Day Event — Sat Jul 25, 11:00 AM — PA
item.description:
Join the City of Lancaster, Let’s Go 123, Lancaster Rec, the Friends of Reservoir Park, and the Pennsylvania Department of Conservation and Natural Resources (DCNR) for an Outdoors for All event on Saturday, July 25, from 11:00am to 3:00pm at Lancaster Reservoir Park, 832 E. Orange St., Lancaster. Launched in 2024, Outdoors for All Day celebrates the value of accessible, welcoming outdoor spaces across Pennsylvania. This year’s event will be a fun celebration featuring organizations from across the Lancaster region that help people connect with outdoor recreation, nature, and community. item.description:
Walking Tails Directions: From the intersection of Egypt Road and Park Ave./Pawlings Road, proceed on Pawlings Road heading towards the Schuylkill River. You will pass Mill Grove on your right, St. Gabriel Hall on your left and Pawling Farm on your left. You are getting close when you pass Sullivan Blvd. on your left and Gertrude St. on your right. You turn left on the next and last left (right before you go over the bridge over the Schuylkill River). Look for the River Trail Valley Forge Park sign visible from Pawlings Road. The gravel parking lot is straight ahead and also visible from Pawlings Road. If you go over the bridge over the Schuylkill River, you have gone too far and are now in Chester county.
CLICK DIRECTLY ON THE MAP IF YOU THINK YOU ARE LOST. IT WILL BRING YOU RIGHT TO US WHERE WE MEET.
This walk goes out about 1.5 miles along the Schuylkill River and then we come back the way we came, for a total of 3 miles. This is a dirt/gravel/mulch trail through the woods.

item.title: Evening Compline — Sun Jul 26, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

The training serves as both the district’s required Valued Volunteers orientation and a kickoff for the Together We Read initiative. Participants will learn about the volunteer process while also receiving reading strategies, tips, and resources they can use when reading with students in our schools. If you’re a first-time volunteer or returning to support SDoL students, the training will provide the tools and confidence needed to make every reading session meaningful.

item.title: Patriarchy, Matriarchy & Democracy: A Two-Part Online Discussion — Thu Aug 13, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Lancaster Freethought Society This is an LFS online discussion series, held on Google Meet. Across two sessions, we’ll explore how patriarchy and matriarchy organize power, care, law, family, sex, money, violence, and democracy. We’ll use consciousness-raising style discussion rules: speak personally, listen carefully, don’t interrupt, and don’t debate someone while they are speaking. For each question, we’ll do a speaking round first. After everyone who wants to speak has spoken, Susan will offer brief evidence, examples, or definitions to deepen the discussion. **Part 1**
* What is patriarchy? * What is matriarchy? * How do these systems operate?
**Part 2**
* What are the benefits of each? * What are the dangers or pitfalls of each? * Can democracy exist inside a patriarchy?
This is not a lecture. It is a structured conversation about power, equality, family, sex, law, care, violence, democracy, and what kind of world we want to build.
Source: Meetup: Lancaster Freethought Socie

item.title: Beginner Birder Trip at East Lampeter Township Community Park — Sun Sep 13, 4:00 PM — PA
item.description:
Sarah Gotwols will lead an afternoon fall migration beginner birder walk at East Lampeter Township Community Park
Celebrate the beauty of fall and the magic of migration with us on a beginner birding program at East Lampeter Township Community Park! Led by an expert from the Lancaster County Bird Club, this walk is perfect for all ages—whether you’re just getting started or want to sharpen your birding skills.
When: Sunday, September 13, 4–6 p.m. Where: East Lampeter Township Community Park (meet at the Lions Pavilion) Register to attend: https://eastlampetertownship.org/departments/parks/#birdwalk
Learn how to use binoculars, field guides, and birding apps—and keep your eyes peeled for a variety of resident and migrating birds on their fall journey. Please bring binoculars if you have them; a limited number will be available to borrow.
In case of bad weather, cancellations will be announced the day before and registered participants will be notified.
Presented in partne

item.title: Ironville Park Raptor Watch — Sat Sep 19, 9:30 AM — Ironville Community Park
item.description:
Carl Groff will lead the count at a hawk watch that will take place in the Ironville Community Park parking lot off Prospect Road starting at 9:30 a.m. The viewing area is level and comfortable. Bring chairs and a lunch. The site has public restrooms and a pavilion. Target species will include Broad-winged Hawk, American Kestrel, Osprey, Bald Eagle and Sharp-shinned Hawk. The watch will continue until the flight ends. Feel free to come and go as you wish. Binoculars are needed and a spotting scope is helpful. Contact Carl at (717-471-9969 or fledge19@verizon.net) by 6 p.m. the day before if you have questions. Prior registration is not required. Location: Ironville Community Park, 711-725 Prospect Rd, Columbia PA 17512 Contact: Carl Groff (717) 471-9969 or fledge19@verizon.net
Source: Lancaster Bird Club

item.description:
Community, Presentation, Adults, Seniors
Are you brave enough to explore the haunted corners of Lancaster County? Join Uncharted Lancaster founder and local historian Adam Zurn for an evening of eerie legends, mysterious happenings, and true tales of the unexplained. This event promises a thrilling blend of history and the supernatural that will leave you glancing over your shoulder on the walk back to your car. From battlefields to backroads, Lancaster County’s long history hides more than a few restless spirits. In the Ghosts, Monsters, and Tales of Adventure presentation, Adam shares some of his favorite stories from his recent book of the same name. The presentation combines historical research, eyewitness accounts, and local folklore to reveal how the past still echoes through the present.Prepare to meet long-dead soldiers, vengeful spirits, and mysterious creatures that haunt the river valleys and hollow hills of the Susquehanna region.
